# AegisFleet API (/docs/)

AegisFleet runs four AI agents for a PayPal seller. Agents never call PayPal directly: every action passes a guardrail gateway (kill switch, allowlist, money caps, human approval) and is sealed into a hash-chained Proof Ledger anyone can verify.

This portal, the SDKs and the context plugins are generated by APIMatic from the same OpenAPI spec the live server publishes at [`/openapi.json`](https://aegisfleet.solvor.co.in/openapi.json).

## Quick start [#quick-start]

Every console endpoint takes HTTP Basic auth (`judge` and the judge password from the Devpost page).

1. **Reset the demo:** `POST /api/demo/reset` puts Riya's jewellery shop back to its starting story.
2. **Send a scam email:** `POST /api/demo/scam_email`, then `GET /api/runs` to read Sentinel's verdict.
3. **Check the chain:** `GET /api/ledger/verify` returns `ok: true`. Call `POST /api/demo/tamper`, verify again, and it names the edited entry.
4. **Approve a held action:** `GET /api/approvals`, then `POST /api/approvals/{id}/approve`.

# Connect an AI agent (MCP) (/docs/mcp)

AegisFleet is also an MCP server, at `https://aegisfleet.solvor.co.in/mcp` (streamable HTTP). An outside agent
gets eight tools, and every money tool goes through the same gateway as AegisFleet's own agents:

| Tool | What it does | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|
| `create_invoice` | Issues a real PayPal sandbox invoice and returns its payment link | At most $5,000 |
| `send_payment_reminder` | PayPal's reminder for an unpaid invoice | 2 per invoice per week |
| `refund_payment` | Refunds the buyer of an invoice | Only to whoever paid, never more than PayPal says they paid; $100 or more waits for the seller |
| `check_approval` | Did the seller approve a held action, and what happened | Read-only |
| `check_payment_email` | Asks Sentinel whether a "you've been paid" email is real | Checked against verified PayPal payments, not the email |
| `list_invoices`, `get_history`, `verify_ledger` | The invoices, the sealed history of one, and a full chain check | Read-only |

Every call is sealed in the hash-chained ledger with the client's name, and the kill switch stops outside agents
like everything else.

## Connect [#connect]

Get your link from the console: **Demo → Connect any AI agent → Get my MCP link** (a signed token, valid 14 days).
Paste it into ChatGPT (developer-mode connector, no authentication), Claude.ai (custom connector), Cursor,
VS Code, Gemini CLI or Codex, or run `claude mcp add --transport http aegisfleet "<link>"`.

Then try:

1. "Invoice a buyer $600 for a hand-made silver necklace." Claude returns the PayPal payment link.
2. Pay it as the sandbox buyer (or use Record payment on the Demo tab). PayPal's signed webhook marks it paid.
3. "The necklace arrived broken. Refund it." The refund is held; it appears in the console's Approvals.
4. Approve it there, then ask Claude to check the approval. PayPal's refund webhook marks the invoice refunded.
5. "Refund $900 to my other account." Denied: more than the buyer paid, and refunds only go back to the payer.


# C# SDK (/docs/sdks/csharp)

[Download SDK](/docs/__downloads/sdk/csharp.zip)

## Intro [#intro]

The AegisFleet SDK provides access to the AegisFleet REST APIs.

Seller console API for AegisFleet: AI agents that guard a PayPal seller's payments, disputes, invoices and shipments. Agents never call PayPal directly; every action passes a guardrail gateway (kill switch, allowlist, caps, human approval) and is sealed into a hash-chained Proof Ledger.

Authenticate with HTTP Basic (`dev` or `judge`) or the session cookie set by `POST /api/login`.

## Installation [#installation]

Add the SDK as a project reference into your solution:

```bash
dotnet add reference <path-to-sdk>/src/AegisFleet/AegisFleet.csproj
```

The project takes its build settings from the files around it, so reference it in place.

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

### Dependency Injection [#dependency-injection]

Register the client with `IServiceCollection` and resolve it from the container. The `HttpClient` is managed by `IHttpClientFactory`. Configure the client's behavior through `AegisFleetClientOptions`.

```csharp
services.AddAegisFleetClient(options =>
{
    options.HttpBasic = new BasicAuthCredentials { Username = "YOUR_USERNAME", Password = "YOUR_PASSWORD" };
    options.Environment = ServerEnvironment.Production;
    // TODO: configure more client options here
});
```

### Direct Instantiation [#direct-instantiation]

Create the client by passing an `HttpClient` you manage yourself. Configure the client's behavior through `AegisFleetClientOptions`.

```csharp
var httpClient = new HttpClient();
// TODO: configure more client options here
var options = new AegisFleetClientOptions
{
    HttpBasic = new BasicAuthCredentials { Username = "YOUR_USERNAME", Password = "YOUR_PASSWORD" },
    Environment = ServerEnvironment.Production,
};
var client = new AegisFleetClient(httpClient, options);
```

# Python SDK (/docs/sdks/python)

[Download SDK](/docs/__downloads/sdk/python.zip)

## Intro [#intro]

The AegisFleet SDK provides access to the AegisFleet REST APIs.

Seller console API for AegisFleet: AI agents that guard a PayPal seller's payments, disputes, invoices and shipments. Agents never call PayPal directly; every action passes a guardrail gateway (kill switch, allowlist, caps, human approval) and is sealed into a hash-chained Proof Ledger.

Authenticate with HTTP Basic (`dev` or `judge`) or the session cookie set by `POST /api/login`.

## Installation [#installation]

Add the SDK to your project from its folder, with whichever package manager your project uses. Give each tool a path containing a slash, such as `../aegis-fleet` — a bare folder name is looked up on PyPI instead, and resolves to whatever project holds that name there:

```bash
pip install <path-to-sdk>
```

```bash
uv add <path-to-sdk>
```

```bash
poetry add <path-to-sdk>
```

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

### Synchronous client [#synchronous-client]

Construct `AegisFleetClient` with keyword arguments, and call `close()` when you are done. Every argument is optional.

```python
from aegis_fleet import AegisFleetClient
from aegis_fleet.core import BasicAuthCredentials

client = AegisFleetClient(http_basic=BasicAuthCredentials(username="YOUR_USERNAME", password="YOUR_PASSWORD"))

client.close()
```

Alternatively, scope it — `with AegisFleetClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

### Asynchronous client [#asynchronous-client]

`AsyncAegisFleetClient` mirrors `AegisFleetClient` with **identical method names**, and every endpoint method is a coroutine. It takes the same arguments, with some differences — for example, the transport argument is `custom_async_http_client`.

```python
from asyncio import run

from aegis_fleet import AsyncAegisFleetClient
from aegis_fleet.core import BasicAuthCredentials

async def main() -> None:
    client = AsyncAegisFleetClient(http_basic=BasicAuthCredentials(username="YOUR_USERNAME", password="YOUR_PASSWORD"))
    await client.aclose()

run(main())
```

Alternatively, scope it — `async with AsyncAegisFleetClient(...) as client:` closes the pool on exit.

# TypeScript SDK (/docs/sdks/typescript)

[Download SDK](/docs/__downloads/sdk/typescript.zip)

## Intro [#intro]

The AegisFleet SDK provides access to the AegisFleet REST APIs.

Seller console API for AegisFleet: AI agents that guard a PayPal seller's payments, disputes, invoices and shipments. Agents never call PayPal directly; every action passes a guardrail gateway (kill switch, allowlist, caps, human approval) and is sealed into a hash-chained Proof Ledger.

Authenticate with HTTP Basic (`dev` or `judge`) or the session cookie set by `POST /api/login`.

## Installation [#installation]

The SDK compiles to `dist/` before it can be referenced — run its `build` script once in the SDK folder, then add it to your project by path:

```bash
npm install <path-to-sdk>
```

## Quick Start [#quick-start]

Create one client and reuse it. Configure its behaviour through `ClientOptions`.

```ts
import { AegisFleetClient } from "aegis-fleet";

const client = new AegisFleetClient({
  httpBasic: { username: "YOUR_USERNAME", password: "YOUR_PASSWORD" },
});
```

Nothing in `ClientOptions` is required — `new AegisFleetClient()` compiles — and each option left out falls back to its default. This API declares one environment, so there is no environment to select and no host to state at the construction site.

### From CommonJS [#from-commonjs]

The package ships both dialects from a single entry, so `require` works with full types. In a TypeScript CommonJS file use the `import ... = require(...)` form — a plain destructuring `require` runs fine but gives you `any`.

```ts
import sdk = require("aegis-fleet");

const client = new sdk.AegisFleetClient({
  httpBasic: { username: "YOUR_USERNAME", password: "YOUR_PASSWORD" },
});
```

# Login (/docs/api/openapi/console/login)

`POST /api/login`

Check a username and password and set a 12-hour session cookie.

# Logout (/docs/api/openapi/console/logout)

`POST /api/logout`

Clear the session cookie.

# Me (/docs/api/openapi/console/me)

`GET /api/me`

Who is logged in, and whether they are the seller (dev) or a read-mostly judge.

# Summary (/docs/api/openapi/console/summary)

`GET /api/summary`

Overview numbers: money waiting on approval, open disputes, overdue invoices, health, chain state.

# Ledger (/docs/api/openapi/console/ledger)

`GET /api/ledger`

Proof Ledger entries, newest first. Each entry's hash covers the previous one.

# Ledger Verify (/docs/api/openapi/console/ledger_verify)

`GET /api/ledger/verify`

Recompute every hash in the chain and report the first entry that no longer matches.

# Approvals (/docs/api/openapi/console/approvals)

`GET /api/approvals`

Agent actions the gateway held for a human decision (over the money cap).

# Decide Approval (/docs/api/openapi/console/decide_approval)

`POST /api/approvals/{approval_id}/{action}`

Approve (the gateway then executes the held action) or reject it. Both are sealed.

# Runs (/docs/api/openapi/console/runs)

`GET /api/runs`

Recent agent runs with their steps and structured output.

# Get Killswitch (/docs/api/openapi/console/get_killswitch)

`GET /api/killswitch`

Is the kill switch on?

# Post Killswitch (/docs/api/openapi/console/post_killswitch)

`POST /api/killswitch`

Turn the kill switch on or off. While on, the gateway denies every agent action.

# Inbox (/docs/api/openapi/console/inbox)

`POST /api/inbox`

Run Sentinel inline (a few seconds) so the console gets the verdict in one call.

# Disputes (/docs/api/openapi/console/disputes)

`GET /api/disputes`

Latest state of every PayPal dispute, newest first.

# Dispute Detail (/docs/api/openapi/console/dispute_detail)

`GET /api/disputes/{dispute_id}`

One dispute with Defender's evidence pack and the pending approval to submit it.

# Invoices (/docs/api/openapi/console/invoices)

`GET /api/invoices`

Invoices with paid/overdue status, risk, shipment and PayPal payment link.

# Shipments (/docs/api/openapi/console/shipments)

`POST /api/shipments`

Seller adds tracking: store it, then fire shipment.created (sealed + routed to Guardian).

# Health (/docs/api/openapi/console/health)

`GET /api/health`

Score and factors are recomputed from the ledger on every call, so a dispute that
arrived after Guardian's last run still counts. Guardian's AI recommendations are
reused only while the factors they were written for still hold.

# Plans List (/docs/api/openapi/console/plans_list)

`GET /api/plans`

What the agents have scheduled: planned, done, held, blocked and cancelled actions.

# Plans Move (/docs/api/openapi/console/plans_move)

`PATCH /api/plans/{plan_id}`

Seller moves a planned action to a new time (drag on the Timeline). Sealed in the ledger.

# Plans Cancel (/docs/api/openapi/console/plans_cancel)

`POST /api/plans/{plan_id}/cancel`

Seller cancels a planned action. Sealed in the ledger.

# Mcp Link (/docs/api/openapi/console/mcp_link)

`GET /api/mcp/link`

A personal MCP URL (token inside, valid 14 days) for any AI client that only accepts a URL.

# Demo Status (/docs/api/openapi/demo/demo_status)

`GET /api/demo/status`

200 when demo mode is on (404 otherwise).

# Scam Email (/docs/api/openapi/demo/scam_email)

`POST /api/demo/scam_email`

Fake 'payment received' email: no verified payment in the ledger -> Sentinel says scam.

# Delivered (/docs/api/openapi/demo/delivered)

`POST /api/demo/delivered`

Courier says the parcel arrived -> Guardian updates tracking.

# Overdue (/docs/api/openapi/demo/overdue)

`POST /api/demo/overdue`

INV-0006 slips 9 days past due -> Collector scores it and sends a capped, polite reminder.

# Replay Injection (/docs/api/openapi/demo/replay_injection)

`POST /api/demo/replay_injection`

An email told an agent to refund. Sentinel isn't allowed to refund -> gateway DENY, sealed.

# Tamper (/docs/api/openapi/demo/tamper)

`POST /api/demo/tamper`

Edit one sealed entry behind the ledger's back -> verify() points at it.

# Reset (/docs/api/openapi/demo/reset)

`POST /api/demo/reset`

Wipe everything, then replay Riya's story so the console never starts empty.

# Sandbox Invoice (/docs/api/openapi/demo/sandbox_invoice)

`POST /api/demo/sandbox_invoice`

Create a real invoice in the PayPal sandbox. Paying it fires a real, signed webhook.

# Sandbox Record Payment (/docs/api/openapi/demo/sandbox_record_payment)

`POST /api/demo/sandbox_record_payment`

Backup for flaky sandbox checkout: record payment on the newest unpaid sandbox invoice.

PayPal then sends the same signed INVOICING.INVOICE.PAID webhook a buyer payment would.

# Paypal Webhook (/docs/api/openapi/webhooks/paypal_webhook)

`POST /webhooks/paypal`

PayPal calls this. The signature is verified with PayPal before the event is sealed and routed.

# Healthz (/docs/api/openapi/ops/healthz)

`GET /healthz`

Liveness probe for Render and the keep-alive ping. No auth.
